1.note: This could mean: (1) a **wind** that was sent in a special way by God, as in the ULT and UST, or (2) a spirit, probably God’s Spirit. Alternate translation: [the Spirit]

1.q: to the eastern gate of Yahweh’s house, facing east
1.note: This gate was part of the wall that surrounded the temple area. Alternate translation: [the gate on the eastern side of the wall surrounding Yahweh’s house] or [the gate on the eastern wall of the temple courtyard]
See how you translated this phrase in Ezekiel 8:16.
The word “behold” here alerts us to pay attention to the surprising information that follows.

1.q: Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah
1.note: These are the names of men.

2.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]

3.q: The time to build houses is not now
3.note: This shows the people feel so secure they are not worried about building houses now. Other versions of the Bible read, “Now is the time to build our houses.” This would mean that the people want to build houses because they feel secure.

3.q: this city is the pot, and we are the meat
3.note: The people speak of themselves as if they were good cuts of meat and of the city as if it were a pot in which the meat was stored or cooked. The metaphor suggests that they are important and safe within the city. Alternate translation: [This city is like a pot that will protect us as a pot protects meat]
This could mean: (1) a pot for storing meat or (2) a pot for cooking meat.

5.q: the Spirit of Yahweh fell on me
5.note: Ezekiel speaks of the Spirit of Yahweh inspiring and empowering him to prophesy as if the Spirit of Yahweh fell upon him. Alternate translation: [the Spirit of Yahweh empowered me]

5.q: That is what you are saying
5.note: “You are saying these things.” This refers to what the people were saying in Ezekiel 11:3.

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [Israelites] or [Israelite people group]

7.q: The people you have killed … are the meat, and this city is the pot
7.note: Yahweh speaks of the people whom they have killed as if they were good cuts of meat and of the city as if it were a pot in which the meat was stored or cooked. See how you translated this metaphor in Ezekiel 11:3. Alternate translation: [The people you have killed … are like the meat in the pot, and this city is like the pot.]

7.q: But you are going to be brought out
7.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But I am going to bring you out]

8.q: this is the declaration of the Lord Yahweh
8.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

9.q: put you into the hands of foreigners
9.note: Here the metonym “hands” represents power or control. Alternate translation: [put you into the power of foreigners] or [enable foreigners to capture you]

10.q: You will fall by the sword
10.note: The word “sword” is a metonym for soldiers who kill people using swords. Alternate translation: [They will kill you with their swords] or [You will die in battle]

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the Introduction to Ezekiel for more information. Alternate translation: [And you will understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [And you will realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

11.q: This city will not be your cooking pot, nor will you be the meat
11.note: The people had spoken of themselves as if they were good cuts of meat and of the city as if it were a pot in which the meat was stored or cooked. Yahweh says that this is not true. See how you translated this metaphor in Ezekiel 11:3. Alternate translation: [This city is not like a pot that will protect you as a pot protects meat]
Alternate translation: [in the land of Israel]

12.note: See how you translated the similar phrase, “you will know that I am Yahweh,” in verse 10.

12.q: the one whose statutes you have not walked in
12.note: Yahweh speaks of obeying his statutes as if it were walking in them, like person would walk along a road. Alternate translation: [the one whose statutes you have not obeyed]

13.note: This phrase is used here to mark an important event in the story. If your language has a way for doing this, you could consider using it here.
This is the name of a man. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 11:1](ta:11).
See how you translated the similar phrase, “I fell on my face,” in 9:8.
The word “Alas” is an exclamation that expresses fear and sadness. Alternate translation: [Oh no, Lord Yahweh] or [Ah, Lord Yahweh]

14.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

15.note: This is stated twice for emphasis.

The word “house” is a metonym for the family, in this case the Israelites who are the descendants of Jacob. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

15.q: All of them are those of whom it is said by those living in Jerusalem
15.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The people living in Jerusalem say about all of them]

15.q: All of them are those of whom
15.note: Some versions have “All of them are those to whom”

15.q: This land was given to us as our possession
15.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has given this land to us as our possession] or [This land has become our possession]

16.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh gives this message to Ezekiel about the Israelites who were in exile.

16.q: I have been a sanctuary for them
16.note: Yahweh speaks of dwelling among the people who are in exile as if he were a sanctuary for them. Alternate translation: [I have been with them] or [I have been like their place of worship]

17.q: I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you from the lands
17.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The repetition emphasizes the surety of Yahweh’s promise to bring the exiles back to the land of Israel. Alternate translation: [I will bring you back from all of the nations]
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [where I scattered you]

18.q: every detestable thing and every abomination
18.note: These words have similar meanings and emphasize that God will remove all the idols from Israel.
This means things that cause hatred or disgust. Here it refers to idols.

19.q: I will give them one heart … give them a heart of flesh
19.note: Yahweh speaks of all of the Israelites who are in exile as if they are one person, with one heart and one spirit.

19.q: I will give them one heart
19.note: Here the metonym “heart” represents the will and emotions. Yahweh speaks of causing all of the people to share the same new emotions as if he were giving them one heart. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

19.q: I will put a new spirit within them
19.note: Here the metonym “spirit” represents the thoughts and disposition. Yahweh speaks of causing the people to think new thoughts as if he were giving them a new spirit. (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

19.q: I will take out the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh
19.note: Yahweh speaks of the people being stubborn as if they had a stone heart and of their being willingly obedient as if they had a heart of flesh. He speaks of causing them to become willingly obedient as if he were exchanging those two hearts. Alternate translation: [I will cause them to stop being stubborn and instead cause them to obey me willingly]

20.q: they will walk in my statutes, they will carry out my decrees and do them
20.note: Each of these phrases have similar meanings and describes the people as obeying what Yahweh has commanded them to do. They are repeated for emphasis.

20.q: they will walk in my statutes
20.note: Yahweh speaks of obeying his statutes as if it were walking in them, like a person would walk along a road. Alternate translation: [they will obey my statutes]

21.q: those who walk with affection toward their detestable things
21.note: Yahweh speaks of a person’s conduct as if it were the person walking. Alternate translation: [those who conduct their lives out of devotion to their detestable things]
This means things that cause hatred or disgust. Here it refers to idols. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 11:18.

21.q: I will bring their conduct on their own heads
21.note: Here the metonym “conduct” represents the consequences of their actions. The idiom “bring … on their own heads” means they will experience these consequences. Alternate translation: [I will cause them to suffer the consequences of their actions] (See also: [Idiom](ta:figs-idiom))

22.note:
# General Information:

The cherubs and the glory of God leave the temple and city.
See how you translated this in Ezekiel 9:3.

24.q: the vision that I had seen went up from upon me
24.note: Ezekiel speaks of the vision ending as if the vision was an object that had been upon him and then left him. Alternate translation: [the vision that I had seen ended]
